title: Two-Sided Bounds on Ground State Properties in Lattice Gauge Theories
authors: Eloïc Vallée, Ariel Kelman, Julius Mildenberger, Jordi Tura, Patrick Emonts
abstract: Gauge theories describe fundamental interactions in the standard model of particle physics and build effective theories in condensed matter physics. Being notoriously hard to simulate, these theories are commonly regularized as lattice gauge theories which can be evaluated with high precision through Monte Carlo algorithms or variational methods. However, Monte Carlo algorithms are not applicable in all regimes due to the sign problem; while variational methods, quantum and classical alike, only give upper-bounds on the ground-state energy. Their precision crucially depends on the chosen ansatz. Here, we present a framework based on a hierarchy of semidefinite programs to yield increasingly good lower-bounds on the ground-state energy and propagate these bounds to extended observables like Wilson loops and mesonic strings. We demonstrate the numerical capabilities by applying the algorithm to a (1+1)-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ theory with dynamic fermionic matter and its pure-gauge version in (2+1)-dimensions. In both cases, we obtain certified intervals for the ground-state energy. For a one-dimensional system with 129 sites, the certified interval has a relative spread of $0.04\%$. For a two-dimensional system with 97 sites (corresponding to a $7 \times 8$ lattice), the relative spread is $2.08\%$. Beyond energy estimates, the proposed method provides rigorous bounds on both short- and long-range observables such as Wilson loops over multiple plaquettes and the magnitude of the mesonic string. The method can be both used as a computational microscope into many-body physics and a way to certify results of quantum simulators.
summary: This paper presents a novel framework to rigorously bound the ground-state properties of lattice gauge theories by combining variational upper bounds with lower bounds derived from Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations. By applying this to Z2 gauge theories in 1D and 2D, the authors achieve certified energy intervals with high precision, offering a powerful tool for both theoretical analysis and validating quantum simulation results.
main_problem: The primary challenge is obtaining rigorous, two-sided bounds on the ground-state energy and extended observables for lattice gauge theories, which are computationally difficult to simulate.
main_result: The authors developed a framework that successfully yields certified, increasingly accurate intervals for the ground-state energy, demonstrated with high precision in both 1D and 2D lattice models.
method: The method combines variational upper bounds (using tensor networks like MPS) with lower bounds derived from Semidefinite Programming (SDP) relaxations based on the NPA hierarchy.
model_or_system: The study focuses on lattice gauge theories, specifically a Z2 gauge theory with dynamic fermionic matter in (1+1) dimensions and its pure-gauge counterpart in (2+1) dimensions.
key_observables: Ground-state energy ($E_{gs}$), Wilson loops, and mesonic strings.
important_parameters: The relative spread of the certified energy interval (e.g., 0.04% for 1D, 2.08% for 2D).
main_assumptions: The Hamiltonian and observables are assumed to be expressible as combinations of Pauli strings, and the method relies on the convergence properties of the SDP relaxation hierarchy.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for bounding techniques, introduces the combined variational/SDP framework, details the application to specific lattice gauge theories, and presents the numerical results demonstrating the certified interval calculation for energy and observables.
why_interesting: The rigorous bounding techniques developed using SDPs provide a powerful, mathematically certified tool to analyze complex quantum many-body systems, complementing direct simulation methods.
